title: EESD surviving-claims robustness across the FEMA P695 far-field set (Ohtori plant)
central_question: Are the two canonical surviving claims (saturation dominates the 2x2 variance; in-QP has a deep-yield failure mode) robust across the FEMA P695 record family, and is the softening-aware null airtight?
architecture: Controllers DESIGNED on the reduced 3-DOF condensed lateral M/K (frozen canonical design points: LQR q=1e12 r=1e-6; softened alpha=0.183); EVALUATED closed-loop on the FULL nonlinear OpenSees Ohtori plant. FEMA records loaded via fema_p695_loader (atc63_norm * global scale).
honesty_scope: Validated BILINEAR plant; drift/accel J1-J6 only (NOT trilinear MEX, NOT damage indices J7-J10). FEMA far-field set is by construction NON-pulse, so 'pulse vs ordinary' is a near-degenerate within-set axis.

subset.rationale: one component per FEMA pair (removes within-pair redundancy); two intensity tiers bracketing onset-of-yield (x1.5, median ~1.9% drift) and deep-yield (x3.0, median ~4.1% drift, 14/22 > 3.5%) where the in-QP failure was observed; 44 evals/cell is enough for the ANOVA share + boundary statistics.
